content: Hydralazine is a medication that can cause several common side effects. These include headaches, decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, a pounding or rapid heartbeat, and chest pain or discomfort. If any of these side effects become bothersome, it is important to inform your healthcare provider. Additionally, there may be other side effects not listed here, so contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing any adverse effects from the medication. Serious side effects of hydralazine, though less common, can occur and require immediate medical attention. These include lupus-like symptoms, which may present as a rash, joint pain, fever, weakness, unusual tiredness, swollen glands, reduced urination, or discolored urine (pink, red, or brown). Swelling may also occur. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Hydralazine can also cause chest pain, which may be a sign of a heart attack. This risk is higher in individuals with pre-existing heart disease. Do not take hydralazine if you have recently had a heart attack without consulting your healthcare provider. Blood disorders are another potential serious side effect of hydralazine. These may include agranulocytosis, anemia, or a low white blood cell count (leukopenia). Symptoms of blood disorders include fever, shortness of breath, pale or yellowish skin, easy bruising or bleeding, frequent infections, unusual weakness or tiredness, dizziness, lightheadedness, or feeling faint. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Hydralazine may also cause nerve problems, such as peripheral neuropathy, which results from damage to the nerves that transmit sensations from the body to the brain. If you notice symptoms of nerve damage, inform your healthcare provider. Certain individuals should not use hydralazine. These include people allergic to hydralazine, Apresoline, or any ingredients in the specific product dispensed. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in the hydralazine product you are prescribed. Additionally, hydralazine should not be used by individuals with coronary artery disease (CAD), a condition where the arteries supplying blood to the heart are blocked or narrowed. This is because hydralazine relaxes blood vessels, which can make the heart work harder and potentially lead to a heart attack. Similarly, individuals with mitral valvular rheumatic heart disease, which involves damage to the mitral valve from rheumatic fever, should avoid hydralazine, as it can strain the mitral valve and increase the heart's workload. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep hydralazine out of reach of children. Be aware that hydralazine can affect alertness or coordination, so avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you know how the medication affects you. Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. This will help determine if hydralazine is appropriate for you. Specifically, let your provider know if you have heart disease (such as coronary artery disease or a history of heart attack), kidney disease, a history of stroke, or rheumatic fever. Hydralazine may interact with other medications and supplements, so always inform your healthcare provider about all substances you are taking. While there are no known interactions between hydralazine and foods or nonalcoholic drinks, it is unclear if alcohol consumption affects hydralazine. Drinking alcohol while taking hydralazine may increase the risk of dizziness. If you accidentally take too much hydralazine, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Hydralazine is available as a liquid for injection into a blood vessel or muscle and as an oral tablet. Always follow your healthcare provider's instructions for use.
